name: CircleCI
scope_notes: Covers CircleCI Cloud. CircleCI cloud (Free, Performance, Scale); SAML SSO and audit log streaming need Scale, context security-group restrictions only on github-type orgs; CircleCI Server is out of scope.

controls.name: Personal API token expiry
controls.what: Every web-created token has an expiry of at most one year; DCR tokens last 90 days.

controls.name: SSO authentication for personal API tokens
controls.what: Tokens must be SSO-authorized per org to reach SSO-protected org resources.
controls.setting: User Settings > Personal API Tokens > SSO column

controls.name: Delete personal API token
controls.what: User deletes a token from the Remove column.

controls.name: Delete project API token
controls.what: Delete a project token (type DELETE to confirm).

controls.name: Project API token scope
controls.what: Choose Status, Read Only or Admin.

controls.name: Context restrictions (security group, project, expression)
controls.what: Limit which users, projects and pipeline conditions can use a context.

controls.name: Rotate/delete checkout or SSH key
controls.what: Delete the key in CircleCI and its public key at the VCS.

controls.name: OIDC trust policy claims
controls.what: Cloud-side trust policy conditions on CircleCI token claims.

controls.name: Pass secrets to builds from forked pull requests
controls.what: OIDC tokens are generated for forked-PR builds only when this project setting is on.

controls.name: GitHub organization deploy key restriction
controls.what: A GitHub org owner can restrict or disable deploy keys across repos, which can disable or remove CircleCI deploy keys. This is a GitHub setting.

controls_unknown: Any org-admin setting to block, list or revoke members' personal API tokens.
Any org setting to disable OAuth Dynamic Client Registration tokens.
Any inbound IP allowlist for the CircleCI API or web app.
Whether personal API token create/delete or API reads appear in audit logs (not in the published event list).
Whether an SSO-authorized token stops working when the IdP session ends or the user is removed from the IdP.

credentials.name: Personal API tokens (incl. tokens from OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration)

authentication.summary: User-created token sent in the Circle-Token header or as Bearer to API v1/v2/v3. Web-created tokens have the user's full read/write access; tokens issued through the OAuth DCR flow are scoped Read/Write/Admin.

federation.details: In SSO-enabled orgs (Scale) a token must be SSO-authorized per org, and that option needs an active SSO session. Docs do not say whether the token stops when the SSO session ends.

ip_restriction.boundary: Docs describe only outbound job IP ranges; no inbound API allowlist documented.

lifetime.summary: User-set expiry up to 1 year; DCR tokens 90 days

renewal.summary: Delete and create a new token; email reminders before expiry.

administration.summary: Users create and delete their own tokens. Any tool can register an OAuth client without authentication and obtain a token once the user approves.
administration.conditions: No documented admin view, revoke or block for members' personal tokens.

sso.details: In an SSO-enabled org, a personal API token must be SSO-authenticated before it can reach the org's resources; SSO needs the Scale plan.

inventory.details: Each user sees and revokes only their own tokens on User Settings > Personal API Tokens; no admin-wide listing is documented.

sso.ui: Org > Single sign-on (SSO) > Enforce SSO for all users; each user: User Settings > Personal API Tokens > pick the org in the SSO column

usage.ui: Org > Security > Audit Logs > Request audit logs > Download logs (CSV); filter on actor. Scale: Stream audit logs to S3

log_sources.name: CircleCI audit logs
log_sources.notes: Org admin requests CSV for any 30-day window in last 12 months (Free 1/day, paid 3/day); Scale can stream to S3.

credential_id_fields.notes: User id/type/name; no token ID documented.

anomaly_cues: Pipelines triggered via API by a user outside normal hours
context.secrets.accessed from unexpected projects or branches
New env vars or project.settings.update by a token owner

containment.steps: User deletes and recreates the token; remove the user from the org/IdP; block new work and rotate secrets the user could reach.

unknown: Whether any API read is logged

authentication.summary: Per-project token with Status, Read Only or Admin scope; works on API v1 only, not v2.

federation.details: Not tied to a user login.

administration.summary: Created and deleted under Project Settings > API Permissions. Deprecated but still in use.

offboard.details: Project tokens belong to a project, not to a user.

inventory.details: Tokens are listed per project under Project Settings > API Permissions; no org-wide listing is documented.

usage.ui: Org > Security > Audit Logs > Request audit logs > Download logs (CSV); filter action project.api_token.create (no field identifies the token on use)

containment.steps: Delete under Project Settings > API Permissions.

unknown: v1 endpoints usable with project tokens

authentication.summary: Each job gets signed OIDC ID tokens in $CIRCLE_OIDC_TOKEN and $CIRCLE_OIDC_TOKEN_V2, issued by https://oidc.circleci.com/org/<org-id>, for exchange with AWS, GCP and others.

federation.details: Outbound federation; the cloud trust policy restricts by claims such as project ID, branch, and context IDs.

ip_restriction.boundary: The relying cloud provider enforces network rules. With the IP ranges feature (Performance or Scale), job traffic comes from published CircleCI ranges that the target can allowlist.

administration.summary: Controlled by the cloud-side trust policy; anyone who can run a job in the org can obtain a token with that org's audience.

network.ui: In .circleci/config.yml set circleci_ip_ranges: true on the job; allowlist jobs.knownips.circleci.com ranges at the target

expiry.cli: Decode $CIRCLE_OIDC_TOKEN and read the exp claim (iat + 1 hour); fixed, not configurable

log_sources.name: Cloud provider logs
log_sources.notes: e.g. AWS AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity; CircleCI side shows job events.

anomaly_cues: Role assumption from projects/branches outside the intended set

containment.steps: Tighten trust policy; tokens expire within 1 hour.
containment.notes: Cloud session credentials last per provider settings.

unknown: Holder calls the cloud provider, not CircleCI

credentials.name: Contexts and project environment variables (stored secrets)

authentication.summary: Third-party secrets stored in CircleCI and injected into jobs. The API returns only names or masked values; the realistic way to read them is to run a job that uses them.

ip_restriction.boundary: The target system enforces network rules. With the IP ranges feature (Performance or Scale), job traffic comes from published CircleCI ranges that the target can allowlist.

renewal.summary: Rotate at source and update the variable.

administration.summary: Any org member can create contexts; contexts default to 'All members'. Admins can add security-group (github orgs only), project and expression restrictions, which combine with AND. Org admins have unrestricted context access.
administration.conditions: Security group restrictions only for github-type orgs.

offboard.details: Secrets belong to the context or project. To use a context, the actor running the workflow must be an org member with access to the context.

inventory.details: GET /context and GET /context/{context_id}/environment-variable, GET /project/{project-slug}/envvar, and the CircleCI Environment Inspector list variable names (values are masked).

network.ui: In .circleci/config.yml set circleci_ip_ranges: true on the job; allowlist jobs.knownips.circleci.com ranges at the target

usage.ui: Org > Security > Audit Logs > Request audit logs (CSV); filter action context.secrets.accessed, target = context

log_sources.name: CircleCI audit logs
log_sources.notes: context and env var change events; context.secrets.accessed.

anomaly_cues: Context accessed by a new project or branch
Masking bypass in step output (base64, reformatting)

containment.steps: Block new work, rotate the secret at its source, update the variable, add context restrictions.
containment.notes: Leaked values stay valid until rotated at the issuing system.

credentials.name: Checkout keys (deploy keys and user keys) and additional SSH keys

authentication.summary: SSH private keys held by CircleCI: deploy/user keys for checking out code from the VCS, and additional keys for deploying to other hosts.

ip_restriction.boundary: The VCS or target host enforces network rules. With the IP ranges feature (Performance or Scale), job traffic comes from published CircleCI ranges that the target can allowlist.

renewal.summary: Rotate by deleting and re-adding the key pair.

administration.summary: Managed in Project Settings > SSH Keys or the checkout-key API. Revocation requires deleting the key in CircleCI and the public key at the VCS.

offboard.details: Deploy keys are not tied to a user. User keys stay until rotated, unless the user revokes the GitHub OAuth integration that created them, which removes them.

inventory.details: Per project only: GET /project/{project-slug}/checkout-key lists checkout keys, and Project Settings > SSH Keys shows all keys.

network.ui: In .circleci/config.yml set circleci_ip_ranges: true on the job; allowlist jobs.knownips.circleci.com ranges at the VCS/target host

usage.ui: Org > Security > Audit Logs > Request audit logs (CSV); filter actions checkout-key.* and project.ssh_key.* (records key changes)

offboard.ui: Project Settings > SSH Keys > user key > X; then delete the CircleCI key in GitHub user settings

anomaly_cues: User keys added (act with a user's VCS access)

containment.steps: Delete key in CircleCI and the public key at GitHub/Bitbucket/GitLab.
containment.notes: Key works at the VCS until its public key is removed there.

calls.reveals: checkout key fingerprints and public keys
